Paytm Merchant AI Hackathon · November 2026

The counter's own AI partner

Vyaapar Saathi reads a kirana's bills, udhaar, stock and supplier quotes — then tells the owner what is costing him money, and does the chasing in Telugu, Hindi or English.

Shri Balaji Kirana · Hanamkonda, Warangal01
The problem

A four-lakh-a-month shop runs on a notebook and a good memory

The udhaar book ₹27,285 outstanding across 16 customers. ₹15,690 of it is older than 30 days, and part of it sits with people who have already stopped coming. ₹15,690
The shelf Seven items run out inside four days. He finds out when a customer asks for milk and there is none. 7
The memory 107 enquiries for 14 products he does not stock. Nobody writes them down, so the same customer walks out again next week. ₹6,373
The buying Four dealers quote on the same 14 items. He buys from the one who delivers, not the one who is cheapest. ₹9,175

Monthly values in rupees. All figures computed from the demo shop in this prototype: 2,577 bills, 45 days, 48 SKUs.

Vyaapar Saathi02
What it is

One agent, three loops: know, act, prove

Know It reads what the shop already produces

Bills, the udhaar book, stock, dealer quotes, enquiries, feedback. No new hardware, no data entry ritual.

Six analyses run every morning: sales, churn, demand gaps, stock cover, udhaar aging, dealer rates.

₹48,115opportunity found in 45 days of one shop
Act It writes the next step, not a report

A win-back message in the customer's language, an udhaar reminder, a purchase order, a supplier quote request.

Addressed to the right person, with the item, the amount and the date already filled in.

3 tapsfrom insight to a message on WhatsApp
Prove Every rupee traces to a bill

The arithmetic is deterministic and sits in one engine. The model chooses words, never numbers.

Every screen carries its source: which bills, which window, which rule produced the figure.

2,577bills behind every figure on screen

The demo · inventory

It knows what is about to run out before he does

₹1.08 L on the shelf

48 SKUs, each with stock, sold-per-day, days of cover and value at cost.

6 items under two days

Bread 0.9 days, tomato 1.1, curd 1.3, milk 1.4. Named before the customer asks.

Reorder that fits the item

Two days of cover for dairy and bakery, ten for staples. Bread gets 11 packs, not 54.

Screen: Vyaapar Saathi prototype. Days of cover = stock ÷ average daily sales over 45 days.

The customer side

Bills on WhatsApp, and a waitlist that closes the loop

01Bill and contactNumber captured at billing with consent; bill sent on WhatsApp.
02Ask and missHe wants something not on the shelf — the ask is logged against his number.
03Stock landsGoods received entry, or the purchase order is marked delivered.
04Agent matchesWaitlist is matched against stock, oldest request first.
05One messageHe is told the item is in, before it goes again.
The message

“Namaste Ramesh garu. The Horlicks 500g you asked for on 12 November is in stock now — we have kept one aside for you till Saturday.”

Live in the prototype: 107 waitlist entries, each with a WhatsApp message written in the customer's language.

Vyaapar Saathi08
The demo · voice

It talks, because he cannot look at a screen

Speak, do not type

A mic on the question box and on the daily check-in, with the transcript appearing live as he talks.

Hear the answer

A listen button on every reply, and a spoken morning brief: takings, what runs out, who went quiet, stale udhaar.

Any mix of language

“Stock ledu em cheyali” is understood as readily as the same question typed in Telugu script.

Production: Sarvam or Bhashini for Indic accuracy, and an IVR number so the owner can simply phone the agent.

Screen: Vyaapar Saathi prototype. Voice runs on the browser speech engine, no key.

Vyaapar Saathi15
Trust and compliance

Nothing is sent without consent, a reason and a person approving it

Consent, per purpose Receipt, reminder and stock alert are separate permissions, each with a timestamp and the language it was given in. Withdraw, delete and export work per customer. 30·22·20
Conduct in code One reminder per customer per week, 9am to 7pm only, no third parties, stop on dispute or hardship. The app never applies pressure; it tells the owner and stops. 1 / week
Human in the loop Every customer-facing message says it was AI-drafted and waits for the owner's approval. Its figures were verified against his own bills before he saw it. 100%
Data and money Numbers masked by default, an audit log of every read and send, no card or UPI PIN ever touched, receipts marked informational and not a GST tax invoice. 0

Synthetic demo data. DPDP Act 2023 alignment here is a design position, not a compliance certificate — confirm the current rules before claiming it.

Why it is worth building

The udhaar book is a credit file

Lending₹27,285 of receivables per shop, aged by actual repayment behaviour. Shared only with a regulated partner, only with each customer's specific consent, never scored by this app alone.partner, not builder
SupplyPurchase orders routed to the cheapest dealer, with the shop's consent. A distribution channel that is already paid for.commission
Payments attach56% of this shop's takings already come through Paytm UPI. Every nudge is a reason to scan again.float and volume
Subscription₹199 a month is our illustrative assumption for what a shop might pay. Not validated pricing, and the last line of the model, not the first.last, not first
